section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the fear in Elul is lower fear, stemming from G-d's greatness within creation, while the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear, stemming from His transcendence above worlds, which can only be attained through a revelation from above.
section.t: And this will be understood by first explaining that the fear of Elul is lower fear, and the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear.
For the difference between lower fear and higher fear is,
as explained in Tanya18
and in many places19,
that lower fear is from His greatness in the creation and bringing into being of the worlds.
For the self-nullification in this fear is the nullification of the sense of self (bitul hayesh).
And higher fear is from His greatness and sublimity that is above worlds,
for everything before Him is considered as nothing.
For the self-nullification in this fear is nullification of existence (bitul bimetziut).
And this is that in order to come to higher fear,
it is specifically through a revelation from above,
because what a person can attain through contemplation is the G-dliness that is relative to the worlds,
and in order for the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds to be felt by him, it is specifically through a revelation from above.
And this is what is stated20
"And the L-rd commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the L-rd,"
that in order to come to fear the L-rd,
higher fear21,
it is impossible to come to this through contemplation, but only through a revelation from above that is drawn down through the mitzvos22.
And this is that the fear of Elul is lower fear, and the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear,
because in Elul,
when the king is in the field,
where being in the field, his greatness and sublimity are not felt23,
and the fear then is
(not from the aspect of revelation from above,
but rather)
through the service of man,
therefore,
the fear then is lower fear.
And on Rosh Hashanah,
when the king is in his palace of royalty,
when his sublimity is felt,
that he is elevated and separate from the people24,
for in the analogue, it is the revelation of the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds,
the fear on Rosh Hashanah is higher fear.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the shofar blast on Rosh Hashanah, being a mitzvah, brings about higher fear, whereas the shofar blast in Elul, not being a mitzvah, only brings lower fear, which serves as preparation for the higher fear.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this that one must blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah in order to come to higher fear,
even though at that time it is a time of the revelation of His kingship,
meaning that in the time of Rosh Hashanah, from its own essence, the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds shines in revelation,
this is,
because time is from the definitions of the world25,
and therefore,
the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is revealed on Rosh Hashanah from the aspect of the time of Rosh Hashanah is related to worlds,
and the revelation of the Ein Sof as it is holy and separate from worlds is primarily through the mitzvos,
"Who sanctified us with His commandments"26.
And since the shofar blast on Rosh Hashanah is a mitzvah,
the fear and trembling from the sound of the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is fear and nullification to the utmost,
higher fear.
And based on this, there is further explanation in this, that the fear that comes from the sound of the shofar of Elul is
(only)
lower fear,
because this that the sound of the shofar of Rosh Hashanah brings about such an immense fear,
nullification of existence
(higher fear),
is from the aspect of the mitzvah of shofar blast,
and since the shofar blast in Elul is not a mitzvah
(and we do not recite the blessing "Who sanctified us with His commandments" over it),
therefore,
the fear
(and nullification)
that comes from the sound of the shofar of Elul is
(only)
nullification of the sense of self,
lower fear.
However, nevertheless,
this fear is an introduction and preparation for the higher fear of Rosh Hashanah,
because in order to come to higher fear, one must first have lower fear
(as mentioned above in the maamar).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that to ascend from lower fear to higher fear, love must first be aroused, as illustrated by the king in the field who receives everyone with a pleasant countenance, corresponding to the two levels of love, leading to the higher fear in the palace.
section.t: And it is known27
that in order to come from lower fear to higher fear, one must first have love.
For the order of service is: fear, love, love, and fear.
Fear
(the first)
is lower fear,
and afterwards, two levels in love,
lower love (ahava zuta) and great love (ahava rabbah),
and afterwards, fear,
higher fear.
And from this it is understood,
that this that from the lower fear of Elul one comes to the higher fear of Rosh Hashanah is through the prior introduction of love.
And this can be explained based on what is stated in Likkutei Torah, that when the king is in the field, he receives everyone with a pleasant countenance and shows a smiling face to all,
for a pleasant countenance and a smiling face are the matter of love,
and by the king receiving everyone with a pleasant countenance,
and especially by showing a smiling face to all,
this arouses in them
(as in water, face to face28)
love for the king.
And based on this, it can be said,
that in the details of the analogy in Likkutei Torah, the four aforementioned matters are hinted at.
For this that they go out to greet the king to receive his face,
pertains to lower fear.
And afterwards,
the king receives them with a pleasant countenance and shows them a smiling face – the two levels of love
(pleasant countenance – lower love,
and smiling face – great love),
and afterwards comes the matter of when he enters his palace of royalty – higher fear.
